title: Open-world long playtest — Guild adventurer progression
brief: Start a genuinely new Avereth campaign at Level 1. Choose your own available base class and two starter skills. Play an independent adventurer in an open sandbox, not a QA script: make becoming a more capable Guild adventurer your central motivation. Actively seek suitable official Guild contracts, gain levels, explore, turn combat loot into money, buy and equip useful upgrades, and pursue real opportunities to learn new skills and improve existing skills. Choose the contracts, class, equipment, skills and route freely. Use available training, teachers, manuals or development offers when useful and affordable; verify that the engine actually grants or improves a skill. Allocate earned stat points thoughtfully. These are ongoing personal goals, not a required achievement checklist. Do not actively seek private quests, private jobs or unpaid routine errands as your main occupation. Incidental NPC help, relationships, paid work and voluntary detours remain welcome when they arise naturally, especially for a sensible immediate need; NPC requests are ordinary world interactions, not formal private quests. Return to your own Guild and character-development ambitions instead of repeatedly looking for another private problem to solve. Prepare before dangerous work: look for local shops and compare affordable weapons, armour and useful supplies early, rather than waiting until a defeat. Make turning combat loot and earnings into usable equipment a recurring personal goal. On an appropriate town visit after successful hunts, actively seek a suitable buyer and sell surplus monster materials and other expendable loot at real offered prices. Keep equipped gear, quest cargo/proof and supplies you still need; do not sell them indiscriminately. Use the proceeds and quest earnings to visit a relevant equipment merchant, request concrete affordable weapon or armour offers, compare them with your current gear, and buy a useful upgrade when one is genuinely available and affordable. Actually equip it and check the engine outcome before relying on it in later adventures; carrying an item is not the same as equipping it. Check what you already own, current HP/MP, recovery options and the cost of food, sleep or lodging. Save for an upgrade or earn money through safer work if necessary; do not repeat shop visits without new money or useful stock. Buy only real available goods at real prices, and verify the engine booked the purchase and equipment. If prices are unknown, ask for an offer instead of merely saying you might shop later. If no suitable buyer, stock or affordable upgrade is available, pursue another sensible opportunity and revisit after circumstances change; do not loop over the same refusal, invent a transaction or buy useless gear just to satisfy the test. Shopping need not interrupt urgent situations or happen every turn. Assess the number and apparent strength of enemies before engaging; a quest label alone does not make a group safe. Choose easier work, recover, withdraw early or abandon a poor plan when sensible. No compulsory or suicidal fights, forced farming, free money, injected XP, fixtures, synthetic gear or invented accomplishments. Retry blocked plans when new evidence or a different approach helps; otherwise find another opportunity instead of repeating fruitless conversations or unrewarded chores. Roleplay and voluntary detours remain welcome. Keep playing naturally through the 100-turn observation window; stop only for death, a genuinely blocking failure or its normal end.

milestones.goal: Create a genuine Level-1 character with your own base class and starter-skill choices.
Keep playing freely until the 100th actual player turn, following your own goals. This is an observation window, not an achievement checklist; do not waste turns to reach the count.

focus: Actively pursue sensible official Guild contracts as a main source of adventure and progression. Choose suitable work freely, verify actual acceptance/progress/turn-in/reward, and change plans when blocked; do not force a particular quest or dangerous encounter.
Notice whether guild membership, rest, sleeping in town, travel, earning/spending money and equipment upgrades are useful and intuitive if they arise.

Act on the loot-to-gear goal during suitable town visits: sell surplus combat loot to a willing buyer, use real proceeds/rewards for a useful affordable upgrade, equip it, and observe it in later freely chosen adventures. Check actual inventory, coin and equipment changes; a narrated sale or purchase alone is not success.

Use genuine opportunities for leveling, useful stat allocation, new skills and improvement of existing skills. Check available skills/training/development offers when relevant, plan affordable preparation and recovery, and verify engine-booked growth. No invented unlocks, compulsory build or fixed training schedule.
Note meaningful inconsistencies between narrator, inventory, HUD, contracts, money, time, NPC actions and engine decisions.
Avoid forcing encounters or repeatedly chasing a fleeing animal just to advance a test. Make believable choices and move on when appropriate.
Keep your messages short and natural. System panels are helpful when needed, not a task to request every turn.
personas: independent cautious Guild adventurer: choose suitable contracts, prepare, recover, sell surplus loot and improve equipment and skills
curious Guild adventurer: freely explore and choose interesting contracts while developing levels, gear and techniques; incidental help remains welcome
pragmatic Guild adventurer: value achievable contracts, loot sales and useful gear or skill investments without reckless fights
